label_note: No source file changes in this world, so a comparison of the code finds nothing. The command first moves existing duplicate rows to a side collection (w004_removed), because a unique index cannot be built while duplicates exist; the revert drops the index and puts the rows back. Idea 91 also changes the seeding script to use a fixed list of URLs; that part is not applied here. Two old behaviours shape this world and were found only by running it: (1) the stored long URL has no path (the URL pattern in src/TextService/TextHandler.h stops at the first '/'), (2) a failed compose is still answered with 200. An answer in case A may name them as further findings.
knowledge_A: The url-shorten store keeps one row for each distinct long URL.
knowledge_B: The url-shorten store keeps one row for every link in every post. Only the short code is unique.
observed_symptom: Run of 2026-11-21. The command removed 49 duplicate rows and built the index. Probes changed: P5 and U1. Posts that carry a link are lost without an error to the client: the gateway answers 200 'Successfully upload post', but the post is not stored and does not appear in the timeline. Logs: url-shorten-service 'E11000 duplicate key error ... index: expanded_url_1 dup key: { expanded_url: "http://example.com" }', then text-service 'Failed to upload urls to url-shorten-service', then compose-post-service 'Failed to send compose-text to text-service'. The effect is wider than predicted: the stored expanded_url is only 'http://example.com', the path is cut off, so every link to a host that was seen before collides, not only a repeated link (P5 uses a new link and failed too). Posts without links pass. Revert dropped the index and restored the 49 rows; clean again.
